hero.title: The paths to fusion power
hero.deck: Explore how fusion machines work, what experiments have shown, and what it takes to turn a reaction into useful electricity.
hero.scope_note: A selected guide to fusion research and development. Results, designs and announced plans have separate labels.

chapters.title: A reaction is the beginning
chapters.deck: The fuel can release energy. A power plant has to capture it, convert it and keep enough to supply its users.

paragraphs.text: Fusion releases energy when light nuclei combine into products with less total rest mass. Many proposed plants use deuterium and tritium, two forms of hydrogen. Their reaction produces a helium nucleus and a neutron, carrying about 17.6 million electronvolts of energy between them.

The fuel becomes plasma: matter containing free electrons and charged nuclei. A useful experiment needs the right combination of temperature, density and heat retention. A very high temperature is only one part of that combination.

In a D-T plant, about four fifths of the reaction energy leaves in neutrons. A surrounding blanket can capture that energy as heat. Electricity production comes later, and the plant must supply its own equipment before it has power left to export.

chapters.title: Different milestones answered different questions
chapters.deck: The history becomes clearer when each result is paired with the question it answered.

paragraphs.text: Laboratory experiments with heavy hydrogen established fusion reactions in the 1930s. By the 1950s, researchers were developing magnetic confinement and working out the conditions needed for useful energy production. The challenge had grown from observing reactions to sustaining the conditions that make them productive.

Tokamak results in the late 1960s changed the direction of magnetic-fusion research. Later experiments improved confinement and explored D-T fuel. JET’s 1997 result reached about 16 megawatts of fusion power from 24 megawatts of external plasma heating. Those numbers describe a plasma experiment’s energy balance.

In December 2022, the National Ignition Facility produced more fusion energy than the laser energy delivered to its target. That crossed an important experimental boundary. The electricity consumed by the laser facility sits outside that boundary, so the result did not establish net electrical generation.

chapters.title: There is more than one way to hold fusion fuel
chapters.deck: The shapes differ because the machines solve confinement, heating and energy capture in different ways.

paragraphs.text: Magnetic-confinement machines use fields to guide charged particles. Tokamaks combine external coils with a substantial plasma current. Stellarators build more of the required field shape into their external coils. Mirrors and levitated dipoles use different geometries, with their own confinement and engineering questions.

In inertial fusion, a small target is compressed rapidly so that fusion can occur before the fuel expands. Lasers may illuminate the capsule directly or first create X-rays in a surrounding cavity. Other concepts use electrical pulses or mechanically compress a magnetized plasma.

A shared label can hide different machines. Helion and TAE both use field-reversed configurations, but Helion pursues a pulsed compression and recovery cycle while TAE uses energetic neutral beams. Their intended commercial fuels also differ from each other and from some present experiments.

chapters.title: Every gain number needs a boundary
chapters.deck: Ask what comes out, what goes in, and which equipment the calculation includes.

paragraphs.text: Plasma gain compares fusion power with external heating delivered to the plasma. Target gain compares fusion energy with energy delivered to a target. Neither ratio automatically includes the electricity used by all the equipment that supplied that energy.

Energy recovery needs an equally careful label. A system can reclaim some energy it previously supplied to its plasma. Realta’s June 2026 direct-conversion experiment predominantly recovered input heating energy. Helion’s current Polaris objective concerns fusion-origin electricity reaching a capacitor bank; its earlier net-electricity wording has been withdrawn.

Net electricity is the remainder after the plant’s electrical consumption is accounted for over a complete interval. For pulsed machines, changes in stored energy also matter. The calculator lets you change these accounting assumptions and see how a positive fusion-gain number can still accompany net electrical consumption.

chapters.interaction_prompt: Move the boundary, then change the illustrative assumptions.

chapters.title: Put each project in its proper place
chapters.deck: Compare the machine, the evidence and the organization before comparing the headline numbers.

paragraphs.text: A company can have several locations with different jobs. CFS is building SPARC in Massachusetts and planning its first ARC power plant in Virginia. Helion’s Everett experiments and its Orion construction site in Malaga are also separate places. The map labels each site’s role and status.

Research laboratories, reactor developers and suppliers contribute different things. Kyoto Fusioneering develops heating, fuel-cycle and plant systems for other fusion programmes. Its engineering facilities belong in the landscape, with a different role from an experiment seeking plasma gain or a proposed electricity plant.

Money also needs a role and a date. A new round may already be included in a cumulative total. Grants, credit facilities and conditional commitments have different meanings. The financing view retains those distinctions, and an undisclosed amount remains unknown.

chapters.next_label: What a plant still has to prove

chapters.title: Several systems have to work together
chapters.deck: A successful experiment can reduce one uncertainty while leaving important plant questions open.

paragraphs.text: A D-T plant must obtain its initial tritium and then produce, recover and recycle enough fuel to continue operating. It must also extract intense heat and manage neutron exposure in its materials. These requirements connect the plasma to the blanket, exhaust, cooling and maintenance systems.

Pulsed plants add questions about repetition, resets and component lifetime. Laser-driven plants also need a dependable supply of targets and a chamber that can accept the next shot. A single successful pulse and sustained power production test different capabilities.

Our assessments describe these questions separately. You can inspect whether a claim rests on an experiment, a subsystem test, a model or an announced plan. We do not turn those categories into a percentage chance of success, and a gap in public evidence is recorded as a gap.

chapters.title: The claims are open to inspection
chapters.deck: Follow a statement back to its source, with the date and qualification still attached.

paragraphs.text: This is a curated research snapshot dated 22 October 2026. Each project-specific claim links to the source used for it. Company reports, laboratory announcements, research papers and programme targets retain their different evidence labels.

A publication date may tell you when a result was reported rather than when the experiment happened. An announced window such as “early 2030s” keeps that wording. Where sources disagree or a financing amount is undisclosed, the qualification stays visible.

Use the source drawer for context and the downloadable tables for the underlying records. The selection is intended to explain the main approaches and the evidence behind them. It is not a complete company census or an investment ranking.

glossary_tooltips.tooltip: Matter containing free electrons and charged ions. Creating plasma does not by itself establish fusion gain.
A form of hydrogen whose nucleus contains one proton and one neutron.
A radioactive form of hydrogen with one proton and two neutrons. It requires controlled production and handling.
A helium-4 nucleus. In D-T fusion, its energy can help heat the plasma.
Fusion power divided by external plasma-heating power, using the stated boundary.
Fusion energy from a shot divided by the driver energy delivered to its target.
Fusion output divided by energy actually coupled into the fuel. Its boundary differs from target gain.
The fraction of driver electrical input that reaches the target or plasma as delivered energy.
Here: gross electricity divided by complete plant electrical consumption over the same interval.
glossary_tooltips.qualification: Site-specific accounting definition; display the actual numerator and denominator.

glossary_tooltips.tooltip: Generated electricity after subtracting all included plant consumption over a complete interval.
Electricity supplied at the grid connection, accounting for imports and changes in stored energy.
Fusion-product heating sustains or propagates the burn under a specified physical criterion.
A plasma strongly heated by its own fusion products. This does not establish an electricity-producing plant.
Density × temperature × energy-confinement time, with the fuel and measurement conventions specified.
A measure of how quickly a plasma loses its stored thermal energy.
How long a discharge or specified operating phase lasts. It differs from energy-confinement time.
Shots or pulses per second, at the stated energy and operating conditions.
A surrounding system that can capture neutron energy, shield components and produce tritium.
Tritium produced divided by tritium consumed, under a stated accounting boundary.
A plasma-exhaust region that handles escaping heat and particles.
A superconducting material used in strong magnets. Fusion HTS magnets still need cryogenic cooling.
A compact plasma configuration with a reversed core magnetic field; it does not specify one fuel or power cycle.
Describes reactions with mainly charged products. Operating plants can still produce neutrons and radiation.
Energy released by fusion, gross electricity and net electricity describe different stages and boundaries.
Reclaiming energy already supplied to a system. Recovery alone does not show new net energy production.
An inferred gain under stated fuel or modeling assumptions. Read those assumptions before comparing it with measured Q.
A plant model’s projected electricity after its modeled internal demand. It is a target until demonstrated.

evidence.label: Measured result
evidence.description: An experimental observation at the stated boundary. Check who reported it and what was measured.

evidence.label: Subsystem test
evidence.description: A component or part of a machine has been tested. Whole-plant performance is a separate question.

evidence.label: Simulation
evidence.description: A numerical result produced under stated assumptions.

evidence.label: Published design
evidence.description: A documented machine or plant concept with projected performance.

evidence.label: Company target
evidence.description: An outcome the developer plans to achieve, with its original timing and scope.

evidence.label: Programme target
evidence.description: An announced objective of a public or collaborative programme.

evidence.label: Reported status
evidence.description: A source describes the project’s condition by this reporting date.

evidence.label: Assessment
evidence.description: An interpretation of the cited evidence and remaining questions; not a success probability.

evidence.label: Not established in this record
evidence.description: The reviewed sources do not establish this result. That does not prove the result is impossible.

evidence.label: Sources differ
evidence.description: The sources give different values or scopes. Open the note to see how the record handles them.

evidence.label: Not applicable
evidence.description: This particular requirement does not apply to the selected role or design.

source_provenance.label: Company report
source_provenance.description: Reported by the developer; independent confirmation is not implied.

source_provenance.label: Partner report
source_provenance.description: Reported by a participating institution or project partner.

source_provenance.label: Laboratory or institution
source_provenance.description: Reported by the institution responsible for the experiment or programme.

source_provenance.label: Peer-reviewed
source_provenance.description: The paper underwent peer review. This label does not by itself establish independent replication.

source_provenance.label: Preprint
source_provenance.description: A research manuscript shared before, or without verified completion of, journal peer review.

source_provenance.label: Company survey response
source_provenance.description: A dated self-reported response within an industry survey.

source_provenance.label: Government announcement
source_provenance.description: The official announcement defines the programme, award or commitment and its conditions.

funding_event_types.label: Financing round
funding_event_types.description: The amount announced for this financing event. Check for extensions or later closing updates.

funding_event_types.label: Cumulative financing
funding_event_types.description: A total reported as of a particular date. It already includes earlier financing within its stated scope.

funding_event_types.label: Grant or grant award
funding_event_types.description: Public or other grant support. The award amount does not necessarily equal cash already disbursed.

funding_event_types.label: Conditional commitment
funding_event_types.description: Financing promised or planned subject to conditions. Keep it separate from completed financing.

funding_event_types.label: Public programme budget
funding_event_types.description: An allocation for a defined programme and period; it may cover several projects or recipients.

funding_event_types.label: Loan or credit facility
funding_event_types.description: Borrowing support. Read the status to distinguish funds provided from an available, undrawn amount.

funding_event_types.label: Government equity-linked award
funding_event_types.description: Public support linked to an ownership interest. The record states whether the award is definitive or conditional.

funding_event_types.label: Proposed merger
funding_event_types.description: A proposed corporate transaction. Its valuation is not cash raised by the company.

funding_event_types.label: Reported cash balance
funding_event_types.description: Cash reported at a specified date, potentially including earlier financing and transaction proceeds; not a new financing round.

dates.label: Event date
dates.description: When the experiment or other event took place, at the precision supported by the source.

dates.label: Published
dates.description: When the source appeared; this may be later than the event it describes.

dates.label: Reported by
dates.description: The source establishes that the status had been reached by this date; the exact event date is unknown.

dates.label: Announced
dates.description: When the plan, financing or commitment was announced.

dates.label: Announced target window
dates.description: A future objective in the source’s own date wording; not an achieved milestone.

dates.label: Research snapshot
dates.description: The cutoff used for this curated dataset.

dates.label: Source checked
dates.description: When the source was reviewed, not independent verification of its underlying result.

dates.label: Date not established
dates.description: No supported date is available in this record.

dates.label: Reported
dates.description: Date of the report; not necessarily the experiment date.

dates.label: Campaign through
dates.description: Month the multi-month experimental campaign ended; exact shot date not established.

dates.label: Undated page
dates.description: Live source reviewed at the snapshot; no publication date established.
